teams.heading: Fiji concede 351 points across their last 11 international matches
teams.body: Fiji have struggled for defensive consistency of late, conceding 351 points across their last 11 games to average 31.9 points shipped per match. In the same 11-match window, the Flying Fijians scored 314 points, yielding an average of 28.5 points per game. This run included their biggest victory of the period, a 63-10 home win over Canada in September 2025 during the knockout stage of the Pacific Nations Cup.

teams.heading: Immanuel Feyi-Waboso shines in freer Exeter role as Steve Borthwick watches on
teams.body: The Exeter winger delivered a standout performance during Friday’s narrow 40-36 defeat to Bath, catching the eye of England head coach Steve Borthwick at the Recreation Ground. Feyi-Waboso excelled in a more liberated role, recording a game-high 132 metres and scoring two tries. While England teammate Henry Slade struggled from the tee, Feyi-Waboso’s "video game stuff" bolstered his standing as a core international starter. With the Australia fixture approaching, such clinical finishing remains vital for an England side seeking consistency.

teams.heading: Exeter Chiefs director Rob Baxter discusses Josh Iosefa-Scott France move
teams.body: The future of Exeter Chiefs prop Josh Iosefa-Scott remains a significant talking point, with the tight-head expected to depart for France when his current contract expires next summer. While reports have linked the 30-year-old with a move to Provence, director of rugby Rob Baxter confirmed that no official destination has been finalised. Baxter noted that while Exeter remains in negotiations, the player has attracted a "very good offer in France" that reflects his consistent form over the past two seasons.

teams.heading: Jane Clohessy earns first Ireland start following family rugby legacy
teams.body: Jane Clohessy made her first start for the Ireland women's side in yesterday's match against Japan at Virgin Media Park. The 27-year-old, daughter of Munster and Ireland legend Peter Clohessy, featured in the second row for the fixture. Reflecting on her transition to the international stage, Clohessy noted, “The whistle goes and you’re straight into it. I feel awful sorry for the girls that are stuck in their own head, I don’t know how I’d cope with that. I’d say it’s the way I’m wired.”

teams.heading: Hector Patterson targeted by Bath amid potential international switch to England
teams.body: Bath are reportedly monitoring Edinburgh scrum-half Hector Patterson as the 21-year-old nears the end of his current contract. While Patterson has represented Scotland at U18 and U20 levels, including a victory at the 2024 World Rugby U20 Trophy, he remains eligible for England through a grandparent. With his Edinburgh deal expiring at the end of the season, clubs across England and France are tracking the son of former Scotland international Derrick Patterson ahead of a potential move next term.

teams.heading: Josh Adams eyes third tournament appearance as World Cup clock ticks
teams.body: Wales wing Josh Adams has declared his ambition to compete at a third Rugby World Cup, aiming for next year’s tournament in Australia. The 31-year-old, who missed July’s defeat to South Africa with a calf injury, is currently working back to full fitness for club side Cardiff. With exactly one year remaining until Wales open their campaign against Zimbabwe, Adams emphasised the need for careful preparation, noting, "I am training, but it's important that you navigate your way through correctly and there's no rush."

lead.why: Josh Adams' explicit target of a third World Cup provides a tangible, forward-looking player narrative.

While the team currently navigates their position in the current log, this past peak remains a significant milestone for Los Pumas in their journey at the elite level of international rugby.

teams.heading: Ardie Savea confirms move to the Blues for 2027 season
teams.body: All Blacks captain Ardie Savea has officially confirmed his return to Super Rugby Pacific, signing with the Blues for the 2027 season. The 32-year-old, who recently completed a sabbatical with the Kobe Steelers, described the move as a long-held ambition. Blues chief executive Karl Budge stated that Savea’s arrival is intended to strengthen the club both on the field and in its efforts to reconnect with the Auckland community following his previous stint with the now-defunct Moana Pasifika.

lead.why: The confirmation of All Blacks captain Ardie Savea signing with the Blues is the most significant domestic transfer news.

teams.heading: Andre-Hugo Venter suffers head injury in Stormers’ defeat against Edinburgh
teams.body: The Stormers’ URC campaign suffered a setback in the Scottish capital as hooker Andre-Hugo Venter was forced off in the 22nd minute following a friendly-fire head clash. Venter failed his HIA and did not return, a development that proved critical as the visitors struggled with a disrupted lineout for the remainder of the 17-13 defeat. The loss of the Springbok front-rower hampered his side’s set-piece efficiency, with the Stormers managing to secure only 57% of their 21 lineout throws.

lead.why: The injury to Andre-Hugo Venter is a direct concern for Springbok depth and marks a significant turning point in a provincial match.
